correctness.rationale: For a minimal Kraus family K_j, the linear map psi -> (⟨G|K_j|psi⟩)_j has rank at most r. If r<d, a unit vector in its kernel is sent to a state supported on G-perp, attaining norm difference 2; the triangle inequality gives the matching upper bound. The exact replacer has Choi matrix I_d tensor |G⟩⟨G|, with rank d. A pure m-mode environment gives at most 2^m Kraus operators after a single coherent unitary evolution and final trace, so uniform error below 2 implies m>=N. In the unconstrained model the exact replacer dilation at m=N can be extended to a joint unitary. Yu–Chen–Lin's model and Theorem 1 provide the stated 2N-mode comparison under their physical hypotheses. No numerical experiment is required.
residual_risks: The lower bound assumes a fixed pure target and uniformity over the full input state space; the bath corollary assumes initial purity and no intermediate discards or resets.

evidence: The entropy bound applies to exact channels and gives r>=d when the maximally mixed input has pure output; the discussion leaves channel-specific approximating rank open.

value.rationale: The result isolates a sharp discontinuity for worst-case cooling: even tolerance arbitrarily close to the maximum yields no environment compression relative to exact replacement. This turns the bath resource comparison into a quantitative statement against the unconstrained information-theoretic minimum, rather than simply restating the exact replacer's rank or counting the modes used by an existing protocol.
residual_risks: There is no assertion that N bath modes achieve cooling under the locality, gap and interaction restrictions of the upper construction.
